summary: Single-panel scatter plot titled 'TensorNet/PBE error geometry colored by bonding class'. It shows per-element elastic-constant errors of the TensorNet/PBE machine-learning potential on a 16-element cubic-metal benchmark: each of 16 labeled points is one element, positioned by its C11 error (x) and C12 error (y) in GPa, colored by bonding class, with a black '1st PC' arrow from the origin showing the first principal component of the error cloud. The dominant structure is asymmetric: 15 of 16 points lie at negative C12 error, most transition metals sit in the both-negative quadrant, and one extreme outlier (Cr) occupies the far upper-right and effectively levers the PC1 direction. Companion workspace files corroborate this reading (feedback_loop_benchmark.json: 16 elements, Cr flagged as extreme projection-residual outlier, Nb also flagged; preprint: the PC1-based global correction operator v0.1 degraded mean MAE to 63.40 GPa and overcorrected Cr).

axes.panels: One panel only; no subplots, no subtitle, no footnote, no sample-size annotation.
axes.title: TensorNet/PBE error geometry colored by bonding class
axes.reference_lines: Grey horizontal and vertical lines through (0, 0) split the plot into four quadrants; a light-grey grid overlays major ticks.

encodings.points: 16 filled circles with thin black outlines, one per element, each labeled with its chemical symbol; no error bars.
color_legend: transition_bcc: Ta, Mo, W, Fe, Nb, V, Cr
encodings.vector: Thick black arrow labeled '1st PC' from (0, 0) to roughly (+48 to +50, +67 to +71), i.e. a slope of about 1.4 in data units, pointing into the upper-right quadrant.
encodings.sign_convention: Per mlip-elastic-benchmark-protocol-2026-06-27.md, error = raw - TPBE_0K (prediction minus 0 K PBE reference), so negative values mean the potential under-predicts that elastic constant.

trends: Strong sign asymmetry: C12 error is negative for 15 of 16 elements (only Cr is positive); C11 error is negative for 11 of 16. The potential systematically under-predicts C12 across nearly the whole grid.

Quadrant occupancy: the both-negative quadrant holds 11 elements (Ta, Mo, W, Nb, Fe, Ni, Pd, Pt, Au, Al, Ca); the positive-C11/negative-C12 quadrant holds 4 (Sr, Ag, Cu, V); the both-positive quadrant holds only Cr; the negative-C11/positive-C12 quadrant is empty.

Clustering: soft, low-stiffness metals (Ag, Ca, Sr, with Au nearby) sit close to the origin; the bcc transition metals other than V and Cr form a band at moderately negative C11 (roughly -18 to -29 GPa) with C12 errors reaching about -40 GPa.

Outliers: Cr is the single visually extreme point, isolated in the upper-right at approximately (+46.5, +80.5) GPa. V is the most extreme positive-C11 point otherwise (about +30, -11). The companion feedback_loop_benchmark.json flags two projection-residual outliers (Cr and Nb); Nb is not visually salient in this figure.

PC1-vs-cloud tension: the '1st PC' arrow points up-right (slope ~1.4) into a quadrant occupied by exactly one point, while the other 15 lie at or below C12 = 0. Geometrically the arrow aligns with the long axis joining the negative-quadrant transition-metal cluster to Cr, i.e. the direction is dominated by the Q3-cluster-versus-Cr contrast rather than a within-cloud correlation most points obey.

Class structure is descriptive only: transition_bcc spans nearly the full horizontal range (W/Mo/Ta strongly negative through V positive to Cr extreme); transition_fcc and noble_coinage_fcc sit mid-cloud; alkaline earths and Al hug the origin.
caveats: Do NOT conclude that C11 and C12 errors are generically positively correlated for this model. The PC1 direction is leverage-dominated by one point (Cr) plus the offset of the negative-quadrant cluster; with n = 16 and a single extreme outlier, PCA direction is fragile.

Do NOT conclude that a global bias correction along PC1 would reduce error. The companion preprint records the opposite: the v0.1 leave-one-out PC1 bias operator degraded mean MAE to 63.40 GPa (vs roughly 13-15 GPa raw) because element-to-element variation in error direction breaks the single-global-bias assumption and it overcorrects Cr. The arrow is a description of the error geometry, not a recommended correction.

Do NOT read this as a bonding-class performance ranking. Class subsamples are tiny and unequal (transition_bcc: 7; transition_fcc, noble_coinage_fcc: 3 each; alkaline_earth_fcc: 2; post_transition: 1); no class means, confidence intervals, or significance tests are shown.

Do NOT equate near-origin position with model skill. Axes are absolute GPa and unnormalized by each element's elastic-constant magnitude: Ag, Ca, and Sr sit near zero partly because soft metals have small elastic constants, while a -30 GPa C11 error for a stiff metal like W is a small relative error. Element-wise quality rankings need stiffness-normalized errors.

Do NOT generalize beyond this exact configuration: one potential (TensorNet/PBE), one cell treatment (1x1x1), one reference (TPBE_0K per the protocol), cubic metals only, and no uncertainty display (the funder brief notes runs are deterministic across 3 seeds, so no sampling noise exists to show, but transfer to other potentials, functionals, or structures is unsupported).

Do NOT infer sample size or outlier status from the image alone. The figure carries no n annotation and no outlier marking; the count of 16 and the Cr/Nb outlier flags come from the companion benchmark JSON, and visual isolation (Cr only) understates the data's flagged outlier set (Cr and Nb).
Do NOT treat the empty negative-C11/positive-C12 quadrant as evidence that sign combination is impossible for the model; absence in a 16-point sample proves nothing.

Do NOT read angles or slopes visually: the x span (~87 GPa) and y span (~135 GPa) are drawn at different data-per-pixel scales, so apparent angles, including the PC1 arrow's visual slope, are not geometrically faithful; the ~1.4 slope figure is a data-unit estimate only.
